FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.94
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not actually run tests against the patched code. In `bench/endocrine.py`, it writes only the patched target file into a temp directory, then executes the caller-supplied `test_cmd` unchanged with `cwd=tmpdir`. The immune pipeline passes `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]` as `test_cmd`. From the tempdir, `bench/tests/` usually does not exist, and even if tests are discovered via imports, the rest of the source tree is not copied, so imports resolve against the original repo or fail. Evidence: patched file path is `tmpdir/basename(target_path)` only; no package tree copy, no path rewrite in `test_cmd`, no `PYTHONPATH` redirection, no patching of sibling modules.
FOLLOW: Downstream, the “sandbox-test proposed fixes” feature does not validate the fix in isolation as advertised. A fix can be marked SAFE/NEUTRAL because tests were not meaningfully exercising the patched artifact, or marked HARMFUL due to path/import failures unrelated to the fix. This crosses the endocrine↔immune interface: Stage 4 in `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` treats SAFE/NEUTRAL as programmatic verification and sets `finding.verified = True`, which then activates NK’s bug-closed gate in later rounds. That can silently close bugs on false evidence or reject valid fixes due to sandbox misconfiguration.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — copy the full relevant source tree into the temp directory, preserve relative paths for the target file, apply the patch inside that copied tree, and run `test_cmd` against the copied paths with `cwd=tmpdir` (or set `PYTHONPATH=tmpdir`). Do not evaluate tests unless they are pointed at the sandboxed tree.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.89
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify a fix as SAFE even when it introduces new issues in one tool, as long as another tool’s count decreases enough to make the summed net negative. Evidence: it computes `total_net = net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues`; if `total_net > 0` => HARMFUL, if `< 0` => SAFE. Example mechanically allowed by current code: `net_type_errors = +3`, `net_ruff_errors = -5`, `net_bandit_issues = 0` yields `total_net = -2` and verdict SAFE despite three new type errors.
FOLLOW: Downstream, fix evaluation can certify regressions as SAFE, and the immune pipeline uses SAFE/NEUTRAL to mark findings verified. That can close a bug even though the proposed fix made the code less type-safe or less secure. Because NK duplicate suppression later treats verified fixes as closed bugs, this propagates a silently wrong verification result across rounds.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — treat any positive per-tool delta as HARMFUL; only return SAFE when every per-tool delta is `<= 0` and at least one is `< 0` or tests passed. Keep per-tool comparisons separate instead of summing them.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.86
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64
DESCRIPTION: FIND — sandbox application loses package structure by writing the patched file to `tmpdir/os.path.basename(target_path)`. If the original file lives under a package path such as `bench/endocrine.py`, the sandboxed file becomes just `endocrine.py`, so static-analysis and any imports evaluate a different module path context from the real codebase. Evidence: `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`; no recreation of parent directories and no copy of package metadata like `bench/__init__.py` or sibling modules.
FOLLOW: Downstream, pyright/ruff/bandit results on the patched file are not representative of the real integration context. Import-based diagnostics may disappear or appear spuriously; relative imports and package-qualified references are evaluated under the wrong path. This makes the endocrine layer’s core promise — “does the proposed fix break anything?” — mechanically unreliable, and that unreliability flows into immune verification and closed-bug state.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — recreate the original relative path inside the temp directory and write the patch there, preserving package layout.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.83
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.43
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `scan_health()` does not report unavailable tools for tools that are skipped due to missing binaries unless an exception is raised. Existing registry already covers the generic availability bug, but there is a second interface hole: the returned `tools_available` map omits tools entirely when `existing` is empty, and omits any tool not iterated or failed before assignment. Consumers therefore cannot distinguish “tool unavailable”, “tool not run”, and “healthy zero diagnostics” from the report shape itself. Evidence: early return `HealthScan(elapsed_s=...)` with default empty `tools_available`; within the loop, keys are added only after runner returns or exception occurs.
FOLLOW: Downstream, callers that rely on `tools_available` as a completeness indicator cannot tell whether the endocrine scan truly covered pyright/ruff/bandit/mypy in a round. For a PoC whole-body monitor, that can mask complete loss of monitoring on empty/misresolved path sets and produce misleading infrastructure health reports.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — always initialise `tools_available` with all expected tool keys set to `False`, then flip to `True` only on confirmed successful invocation.
VERIFIED: TRUE

EXTEND C0021 | Timeout handling is not just a health-scan parsing issue. The same `_run_tool` sentinel behavior also contaminates fix evaluation baselines and post-fix counts via `_count_tool_issues(run_pyright/run_ruff/run_bandit, file_path)`. A timed-out tool currently returns `[]`, which looks like “0 issues”, so a slow analysis can make harmful fixes appear neutral/safe.

EXTEND C0005 | The dead/partial feature set also includes the fix-evaluation promise in the module docstring: “sandbox-test proposed fixes” claims no source modification and representative validation, but implementation only writes a single basename file into tempdir and does not sandbox tests against the patched tree. This is not just missing categories; one advertised core capability only partially fires.
